February 10

7 For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice, 8 Harden not your heart, as in the provocation, and as in the day of temptation in the wilderness: 9 When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my work. 10 Forty years long was I grieved with this generation, and said, It is a people that do err in their heart, and they have not known my ways: 11 Unto whom I sware in my wrath that they should not enter into my rest. (Psalms 95:7-11 KJV)

Many times the bible refers to us as the sheep and God, or Jesus, as our Shepherd (i.e. John 10:14). We are to be like sheep, and follow after our Shepherd, and not stray off the path of righteousness. The Jews, even after seeing the marvelous things that God did in bringing them out of Egypt, did nothing but complain and hardened their hearts toward God. Then they refused to enter into the Promised Land that God wanted to give them, and provoked God, making them spend 40 years in the wilderness. God was truly grieved with them, and I am sure He gets grieved with us, His children.

We need to always love our God with all our hearts (Matthew 22:37), and never to grieve Him. He is so good to all of us, and if He were not so longsuffering with us, we would all be a pile of ashes by now. We are now in God’s rest (Hebrew 4:10), thanks to the sacrifice that Jesus made for us, as we no longer have to do the works of the law, and try to justify ourselves. We have been given the righteousness of Jesus by grace (Romans 3:22), so we do not have to try and earn anything from God. Jesus has already obtained all spiritual blessings for us (Ephesians 1:3), and all we need to do is find out what we already have, and how to use it. We are to rest from our works, and that means we need to quit trying to earn our way to heaven, but need to put all our faith into the grace of God, that Jesus brought to us. Thank you Jesus!
